items.title: UK and allies say Navalny was killed with rare dart frog toxin

featured_image.name: UK, allies say they're convinced Kremlin critic Navalny was poisoned

items.description:
Russian opposition leader Alexei Navalny was poisoned with epibatidine, a lethal toxin found in South American poison dart frogs, according to a joint announcement by five European nations on the second anniversary of his death in a Siberian penal colony.

The United Kingdom, France, Germany, Sweden, and the Netherlands issued a joint statement on Saturday confirming that analyses of samples from Navalny "conclusively confirmed the presence of epibatidine," a substance not found naturally in Russia. The announcement, made at the Munich Security Conference, directly implicates the Russian government in Navalny's death, with the coalition stating that "only the Russian state had the combined means, motive and disregard for international law" to carry out the attack.[1][2][3]

items.title: Rubio urges transatlantic unity as Europe stresses self-reliance

featured_image.name: In Munich, Rubio urges transatlantic unity but lashes Europe on migration

items.description:
The 62nd Munich Security Conference opened this weekend to a fractured Western alliance, with European leaders delivering pointed assessments of transatlantic relations while U.S. Secretary of State Marco Rubio attempted to reassure anxious allies that Washington still values its oldest partnerships.

German Chancellor Friedrich Merz set the tone on Friday when he declared that the rules-based world order "no longer exists" and acknowledged that "a deep divide has opened between Europe and the United States." Speaking directly to the American delegation, Merz warned that U.S. claims to global leadership have been "challenged, and possibly lost," while urging Europe to stop denying the scale of the geopolitical challenge it faces.[1][2]

items.title: Iran arrests over 50,000 in dragnet after deadly protest crackdown

featured_image.name: Arrests of protestors continue to roil Iran weeks after ...

items.description:
Iranian security forces have arrested more than 50,000 people in a sweeping campaign following a brutal crackdown last month that killed thousands of demonstrators, according to human rights groups. The dragnet, spanning major cities and rural towns, has targeted protesters, doctors, lawyers, students, actors, and reformist political figures, with many held incommunicado for days or weeks.[1][2]

The Associated Press reported that security agents have conducted late-night raids on homes and workplaces across the country, using surveillance footage and facial recognition technology to track down individuals who participated in protests that peaked in early January.[2][3]

items.title: NASA reviews Artemis II test data as moon mission eyes March

featured_image.name: More trouble for Artemis-II rocket, Moon launch likely delayed again

items.description:
NASA engineers are analyzing data from a confidence test conducted on February 12 as the agency works toward returning humans to the Moon for the first time in more than five decades. The test was designed to evaluate repairs made following a hydrogen leak that forced NASA to push back the Artemis II launch from its original February window.

During the test at Kennedy Space Center, operators partially filled the Space Launch System core stage liquid hydrogen tank to assess newly replaced seals in the propellant fueling area, NASA said in a statement. Teams encountered an issue with ground support equipment that reduced the flow of liquid hydrogen into the rocket, though engineers were able to achieve several key objectives and collect data at the same point in testing where a leak had been detected during the previous wet dress rehearsal.[1][2]

items.title: SpaceX Crew-12 to dock with ISS on Valentine's Day

featured_image.name: NASA and SpaceX set to launch Crew-12 to the ISS on Feb 13 ...

items.description:
A SpaceX Falcon 9 rocket lifted off early Friday morning carrying four astronauts toward the International Space Station, marking the 12th operational crew rotation mission under NASA's Commercial Crew Program. The Crew Dragon capsule "Freedom" is set to dock with the orbiting outpost this afternoon, delivering a relief crew after an unprecedented medical evacuation last month left the station short-staffed.

The mission launched at 5:15 a.m. EST on February 13 from Space Launch Complex 40 at Cape Canaveral Space Force Station in Florida. The crew consists of NASA astronauts Jessica Meir, serving as commander, and Jack Hathaway as pilot, along with mission specialists Sophie Adenot of the European Space Agency and Andrey Fedyaev of Roscosmos.[1][2][3]

items.title: NASA extracts oxygen from lunar soil using solar energy

featured_image.name: Sunlight extracts oxygen from regolith using solar chemistry

items.description:
NASA has achieved a milestone in lunar resource utilization, completing integrated prototype testing that used concentrated solar energy to extract oxygen from simulated lunar soil. The Carbothermal Reduction Demonstration project, known as CaRD, confirmed the production of carbon monoxide through a solar-driven chemical reaction, marking a key advance toward sustaining human exploration on the Moon.[1][2]

The successful test represents a step toward enabling astronauts to produce propellant using only lunar materials and sunlight, which could reduce the cost and complexity of maintaining a long-term presence on the lunar surface. The same technology could eventually be adapted to convert carbon dioxide into oxygen and methane on Mars.[2][3]

items.title: Cornell study pinpoints global crop emissions to 10-kilometer resolution

featured_image.name: What's the Climate Cost of Growing Crops? - World Resources Institute

items.description:
Researchers have produced the most comprehensive map of global cropland greenhouse gas emissions to date, revealing that just four crops—rice, maize, oil palm, and wheat—account for nearly three-quarters of all emissions from farming, with rice alone responsible for 43%.

The study, published February 13 in Nature Climate Change, synthesizes data from ground measurements, remote sensing, inventory surveys, and hydrological models to achieve a spatial resolution of approximately 10 kilometers—enabling emissions to be pinpointed not just by country, but by individual crops and management practices.[1][2]

items.title: Blue Origin reveals accelerated Moon plan as SpaceX pivots from Mars

featured_image.name: Why Did Jeff Bezos Post a Turtle Image on X? And Why Is Elon ...

items.description:
The race to return humans to the lunar surface has entered a new phase this week, with both SpaceX and Blue Origin unveiling aggressive strategies to beat China to the Moon, while Beijing continues to make steady progress toward its 2030 landing goal.

On February 9, Elon Musk announced a dramatic shift in SpaceX's priorities, revealing that the company has pivoted toward building a "self-growing city" on the Moon within the next decade. The announcement, made on his social media platform X, marks a stark reversal for the billionaire, who as recently as last year dismissed lunar missions as a "distraction" from his Mars ambitions. According to Reuters, Musk said traveling to Mars is only possible every 26 months, while launches to the Moon can occur every 10 days, allowing SpaceX to "iterate much faster."[1][2][3]

items.title: Zelensky says Ukraine won't hold referendum on 'bad' peace deal

featured_image.name: Zelensky gives major update on potential Ukraine peace deal ...

items.description:
Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky offered a detailed account of his approach to peace negotiations with Russia in an exclusive interview with The Atlantic, published Thursday as he prepared to attend the Munich Security Conference. Speaking with journalist Simon Shuster, Zelensky emphasized Ukraine's willingness to engage constructively with U.S.-led proposals while setting firm conditions for any final agreement.

"The tactic we chose is for the Americans not to think that we want to continue the war," Zelensky told The Atlantic. "That's why we started supporting their proposals in any format that speeds things along."[1][2]

items.title: Trump sends second carrier to Gulf as Iran fortifies nuclear site

featured_image.name: Trump sends second aircraft carrier to Gulf amid Iran threats

items.description: Iran is reinforcing tunnel entrances at a major underground complex near its Natanz nuclear facility, according to new satellite imagery analyzed by the Institute for Science and International Security (ISIS), a U.S.-based think tank. The developments come as the Trump administration deploys additional military assets to the Middle East and nuclear negotiations between Washington and Tehran hang in the balance.

items.title: Fire erupts at Havana refinery as Cuba endures US oil blockade

featured_image.name: Western Cuba faces blackout as government seeks to update energy grid

items.description:
A fire erupted Friday at the Ñico López refinery in Havana Bay, dealing another blow to Cuba as the island nation struggles with an intensifying energy crisis caused by a U.S.-imposed oil blockade. Dense black smoke was seen rising from the facility, though authorities have not confirmed casualties or damage to oil storage tanks.[1][2]

The blaze comes as Cuba has gone a full month without a major fuel delivery, according to data analytics firm Kpler cited by Bloomberg. Since the Trump administration's January 29 executive order threatening tariffs on any nation supplying oil to Cuba, the island's two primary suppliers—Venezuela and Mexico—have halted shipments, leaving the country's aging power infrastructure starved of the roughly 100,000 barrels of crude it needs daily.[3][4]

items.title: Macron urges Europe to become a geopolitical power at Munich

featured_image.name: Germany and France now publicly display their disagreements over Macron's proposals

items.description:
French President Emmanuel Macron called on Europe to embrace its role as a geopolitical power and define its own security future in a keynote speech at the Munich Security Conference on Friday, delivering a pointed defense of the continent amid shifting transatlantic dynamics.

"This is the right time for audacity. This is the right time for a strong Europe," Macron declared, urging European leaders to shed self-doubt. "Europe has to learn to become a geopolitical power. It was not part of our DNA."[1][2]

items.title: Yangtze fishing ban halts 70 years of biodiversity decline

featured_image.name: Five Years Into a Fishing Ban, the Yangtze River Is Teeming ...

items.description: China's decade-long commercial fishing ban on the Yangtze River has halted 70 years of biodiversity decline and triggered early signs of ecological recovery, according to a comprehensive study published this week in the journal Science. Fish biomass has more than doubled, endangered species are rebounding, and the world's longest river system appears to be making a cautious comeback.[1]

items.title: Trump tells Zelenskyy to 'get moving' as Geneva talks set

featured_image.name: Trump, Zelenskyy meeting shocks Europe, delights Russia ...

items.description:
President Donald Trump issued an urgent public warning to Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy on Friday, saying his counterpart must "get moving" on peace negotiations with Russia or risk missing a historic opportunity to end the nearly four-year conflict. The remarks came as both nations confirmed a third round of U.S.-brokered talks will take place in Geneva next week.

"Russia wants to make a deal, and Zelenskyy's gonna have to get moving—otherwise he's going to miss a great opportunity. He has to move," Trump told reporters while leaving the White House.[1][2]

The Trump administration is pushing for a peace agreement by early summer, with Zelenskyy himself acknowledging last week that U.S. officials want the war concluded by June. In remarks to reporters in Kyiv, Zelenskyy said he understands the reasoning: American attention will soon shift to the November congressional midterm elections.[3][4]

"The Americans are proposing the parties end the war by the beginning of this summer and will probably put pressure on the parties precisely according to this schedule," Zelenskyy said, adding candidly, "The elections are undoubtedly more significant for them. Let's not be naive".[5][4]

items.title: Nvidia shares stall as insiders sell $100M despite AI boom

featured_image.name: Nvidia stock jumps 4% before CEO Jensen Huang's CES keynote

items.description:
Nvidia shares have traded sideways in recent weeks, hovering near $185, even as major cloud providers announced record capital expenditure plans totaling nearly $700 billion for artificial intelligence infrastructure in 2026. The chipmaker is scheduled to report fourth-quarter fiscal 2026 results on February 25, with Wall Street expecting revenue of approximately $65 billion.

The disconnect between Nvidia's stock performance and the explosive growth in AI spending by its biggest customers has puzzled some investors. Amazon, Alphabet, Meta, and Microsoft collectively plan to spend between $635 billion and $665 billion this year, a roughly 70% increase from 2025, according to Yahoo Finance. The majority of this investment is directed toward AI chips, server infrastructure, and data center development.[1]

items.title: China's Yangtze fishing ban doubles fish biomass, study finds

featured_image.name: Five Years Into a Fishing Ban, the Yangtze River Is Teeming ...

items.description:
China's sweeping 10-year commercial fishing ban on the Yangtze River has halted seven decades of biodiversity decline, with fish biomass more than doubling and endangered species showing signs of recovery, according to new research published Thursday in the journal Science.[1]

The study, which analyzed fish communities across 57 river reaches from 2018 to 2023, found that overall fish biomass increased by 209% and species richness rose by 13% following the implementation of the fishing ban in 2021. The recovery has been particularly pronounced among larger-bodied fish species occupying higher positions in the food web, including economically valuable species such as the black Amur bream and white Amur bream.[2][1]

items.title: Musk's bankers work to refinance $18B debt ahead of SpaceX IPO

featured_image.name: SpaceX hits €1.06tn after xAI merger as Musk consolidates ...

items.description:
Elon Musk's banking team is working on a potential financing strategy that could reduce the heavy interest burden the billionaire has accumulated through years of acquisitions, according to Bloomberg.[1]

The refinancing effort comes less than two weeks after SpaceX officially completed its merger with xAI on February 2, creating the world's most valuable private company with a combined valuation of approximately $1.25 trillion. The all-stock deal positioned the new entity ahead of what is expected to be one of the largest initial public offerings in history later this year.[2][3]

items.title: Trump administration escalates pressure on Ukraine for peace deal

featured_image.name: Trump Gives New Deadline for Ending Russia-Ukraine War: Zelensky

items.description:
The Trump administration is intensifying demands on Ukraine to accept territorial compromises and hold elections to end the war with Russia by early summer, according to Ukrainian officials cited by The New York Times on Friday.[1][2]

The pressure comes as Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky and US Secretary of State Marco Rubio are set to meet at the Munich Security Conference, which begins February 13. Ukrainian officials reported that Washington is pushing harder on Kyiv than on Moscow to reach a settlement before the November US midterm elections, with negotiations potentially resuming as early as next week.[3][1]

items.title: Yangtze fish biomass more than doubled after five-year ban

featured_image.name: China's endangered Yangtze finless porpoise swims back from ...

items.description:
Fish biomass in China's Yangtze River has more than doubled and endangered species populations are recovering, according to new research documenting the effects of an unprecedented decade-long commercial fishing ban that began in 2021.

A peer-reviewed study published Thursday in the journal Science found that the full fishing ban has halted seven decades of biodiversity decline in Asia's longest river, with fish biomass increasing by a median of 209% and species richness rising by 13%. The findings arrive as China marks the halfway point of its ambitious conservation effort, which required resettling more than 231,000 fishers and recalling 111,000 fishing boats at a cost exceeding $2.74 billion.[1]

items.title: Germany's Merz rebukes 'MAGA culture war' at Munich conference

featured_image.name: Merz: Old world order 'no longer exists,' great power ...

items.description:
German Chancellor Friedrich Merz opened the Munich Security Conference on Friday by acknowledging a deep divide between the United States and Europe while urging both sides to rebuild trust through a new partnership framework.

In his keynote address, Merz warned that the post-World War II international order "no longer exists in that form" and called on European nations to strengthen their defense capabilities while keeping the transatlantic alliance intact.[1][2]

"A rift has opened up between Europe and the United States," Merz said, directly referencing Vice President JD Vance's confrontational speech at the same conference a year earlier. But he pushed back sharply against the cultural criticisms Vance leveled at European governments: "The culture war of the MAGA movement is not ours. Freedom of speech ends here with us when that speech goes against human dignity and the constitution."[2]
